title: [Keyboard Manager] the new editor doesn't show targeted process name for disabled chords
author: thefasquelle
summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor omits the targeted process name for app-specific disabled shortcuts/chords and can lose specificity when converting a disabled chord to a disabled key.

confidence.rationale: The public reproduction localizes the missing metadata path, but code inspection must confirm whether display and conversion share one mapper or two defects.

judgment.rationale: The report includes exact steps, a screenshot, diagnostics, and independent confirmation on 0.100.2. The symptom is localized to disabled-remap presentation and conversion in the new editor.
evidence: An app-specific ordinary remap displays its target, while an app-specific disabled chord does not.
The reporter supplied a screenshot and a PowerToys bug-report ZIP.
A current 0.100.2 confirmation also found that converting an app-specific disabled chord to a disabled key breaks specificity.
judgment.recommended_action: Preserve and render target-application metadata for disabled entries across list display and chord-to-key conversion.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The UI omission and data-loss observation point to the same metadata plumbing boundary. The fix should cover both rendering and edit/conversion serialization rather than only adding a label.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve target application metadata for disabled remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The new editor's disabled-shortcut/key representation or list-item mapper does not consistently carry the target process field used by normal app-specific remaps.
plan: Trace disabled chord/key models through editor loading, list-item projection, and save/conversion code.
Include target application in disabled-entry display and preserve it when converting between disabled chord and disabled key.
Add round-trip tests for global and app-specific disabled entries and UI assertions for the displayed process name.
verification: Create app-specific ordinary, disabled-chord, and disabled-key remaps and confirm every list row displays the same target.
Convert the disabled chord to a disabled key, save/reopen the editor, and confirm the target scope and runtime behavior remain app-specific.

confidence.rationale: The public reproduction localizes the missing metadata path, but code inspection must confirm whether display and conversion share one mapper or two defects.

issue_context.summary: The new Keyboard Manager editor omits the targeted process name for app-specific disabled shortcuts/chords and can lose specificity when converting a disabled chord to a disabled key.
known_information: The issue affects the new/default Keyboard Manager editor.
The target application is configured but absent from the disabled-chord list display.
The conversion path can change an app-specific disabled chord into a key while losing application scope.
inferences: Disabled entries likely use a specialized view model or conversion path that omits the target process field used by ordinary remaps.
issue_context.analysis: The UI omission and data-loss observation point to the same metadata plumbing boundary. The fix should cover both rendering and edit/conversion serialization rather than only adding a label.

reproduce.title: Round-trip app-specific disabled remaps in the new editor
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: A harmless target such as notepad.exe
setup: Create one app-specific ordinary shortcut remap and one app-specific disabled chord for the same target.
steps: Compare the target-process text shown in both rows.
Edit the disabled chord into a disabled key and save.
Reopen the editor and test the disabled key inside and outside the target app.
